source: current independent re-fetch of the official NSF award API and program solicitation

claims.statement: NSF award 2616828 identifies Rice University as the awardee and Hengrui Luo as principal investigator.
claims.quote: agency: NSF; id: 2616828; awardeeName: William Marsh Rice University; awardeeCity: HOUSTON; awardeeStateCode: TX; piFirstName: HENGRUI; piLastName: LUO
claims.source_type: National Science Foundation official award API
claims.note: Rice University is in Houston, Harris County; the university faculty profile independently confirms Luo's Rice appointment.

claims.statement: The award was dated August 17, 2026 and its funded term starts September 15, 2026.
claims.source_type: National Science Foundation official award API
claims.note: The September 15 date is a start date, not proof that experiments or software have already begun.

claims.statement: The current NSF record lists 150,000 dollars in obligated funds for the Rice award.
claims.source_type: National Science Foundation official award API
claims.note: This is the current obligated amount, not a valuation of resulting software.

claims.statement: The project targets numerical linear algebra, which the award describes as foundational to scientific simulation, data analysis and AI.
claims.quote: Numerical linear algebra (NLA) is foundational to mathematical and statistical computing, scientific simulation, data analysis, and artificial intelligence.
claims.source_type: National Science Foundation official award API
claims.note: Foundational does not mean every named application will use the eventual research outputs.

claims.statement: The award says reinforcement learning and large language models can explore algorithm designs efficiently but may produce opaque or inconsistent results without guarantees.
claims.quote: AI methods, including reinforcement learning (RL) and large language models (LLMs), can explore algorithm designs efficiently, but they may produce opaque or inconsistent results without dependable guarantees.
claims.source_type: National Science Foundation official award API
claims.note: The project is designed around this limitation; it does not establish that a particular model has already failed.

claims.statement: LAAM will represent each candidate as a structured mathematical derivation recording transformations, loops, primitives, parameters and symbolic costs.
claims.quote: LAAM will represent each candidate as a structured mathematical derivation that records algebraic transformations, nested-loop organization, compositional primitives, admissible parameters, and symbolic arithmetic and communication costs.
claims.source_type: National Science Foundation official award API
claims.note: Will represent is a stated research design, not a completed artifact.

claims.statement: The project plans Bayesian optimization and reinforcement learning methods to find promising distinct candidates while limiting expensive proof and evaluation calls.
claims.quote: identify promising and mathematically distinct candidates while minimizing expensive proof and evaluation calls
claims.source_type: National Science Foundation official award API

claims.statement: Lean is planned to certify deterministic correctness and cost claims before AI-generated candidates become reusable mathematical objects.
claims.quote: Lean will certify deterministic correctness and cost claims, thereby converting AI-generated candidates into reusable mathematical objects rather than opaque algorithmic programs. Finally, a verified mathematical library will attach machine-readable accuracy, precondition, cost, and confidence contracts to certified routines and record certificate-backed provenance.
claims.source_type: National Science Foundation official award API
claims.note: Lean is the proof assistant named in the award; certification is a planned condition, not an already published result.

claims.statement: The project treats prompt-to-prompt variation as a measurement problem and plans inference to distinguish genuine improvements from model-induced randomness.
claims.quote: Because LLM-generated algorithms and proofs vary across prompts, the LAAM will also develop sequentially valid inference to separate genuine algorithmic improvements from model-induced randomness.
claims.source_type: National Science Foundation official award API
claims.note: The award does not publish a finished evaluation result.

claims.statement: The award names possible applications including principal component analysis, least squares, regression, low-rank approximation and matrix completion.
claims.quote: principal component analysis, least squares, regression, low-rank approximation, and matrix completion
claims.source_type: National Science Foundation official award API
claims.note: These are intended application areas, not documented deployments.

claims.statement: The award promises openly available software and educational materials and public workshops.
claims.quote: The investigators will release openly available software and educational materials, host public workshops, and broaden participation.
claims.source_type: National Science Foundation official award API
claims.note: The record gives no release dates or workshop dates.

claims.statement: NSF's program requires collaboration between scientific computing and formal reasoning expertise and puts correctness on equal footing with performance.
claims.quote: The CS2 program puts correctness on an equal footing with performance
claims.source_title: NSF 24-571: Correctness for Scientific Computing Systems
claims.note: This describes the funding program, not a measured result from the Rice award.

rejected_or_unsupported: No claim that LAAM software already exists or has produced a new algorithm.
No claim that the project has improved the speed or reliability of a named deployed system.
No claim that Lean independently evaluates real-world usefulness; the record limits its stated role to formal correctness and cost claims.
No claim that the public can comment on or apply to the award.
